privacy.ai_training_note: Warp's privacy policy lists model training as a stated purpose: 'Develop new products and Service, and improve existing products and features of the Service, including by training, fine-tuning and improving the performance of models that support our AI features.' The policy also states that when using AI features such as Active AI and Agent Mode, 'we may collect the prompts and inputs you submit and the outputs you receive. You can control our collection of these inputs and outputs at any time in your settings.' So on consumer/free plans, prompt/input collection (and potential use for improving models) is on by default but user-controllable. A Zero Data Retention (ZDR) policy is available only on the Enterprise plan, and all users can opt out of telemetry while still using AI. Enterprise admins can enforce disabling Warp AI / telemetry / secret redaction.
privacy.data_region: United States (Google Cloud Platform; database locations in the US). Warp AI requests proxied to US-hosted, enterprise-level model APIs.

security.value: Google Cloud Platform, US database locations

security.name: Penetration testing

products.name: Warp Terminal (free / Pro)
products.data_scope: Local terminal app with cloud features. Prompts/inputs to AI features may be collected (user-controllable); telemetry opt-out available. No ZDR on free/Pro tiers.
products.notes: Now open-source. Most consumer usage; default AI input collection is the key privacy consideration.

products.name: Warp AI / Warp Agent
products.data_scope: AI requests proxied to US-hosted enterprise model APIs. Prompts and outputs may be collected unless disabled. Access to multiple frontier models with permission controls.
products.notes: Privacy policy lists model fine-tuning/improvement as a purpose. ZDR only on Enterprise.

products.name: Warp Drive
products.data_scope: Workflows, notebooks, shared blocks stored in GCP (US). Encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3).

products.name: Oz (cloud agent orchestration)
products.data_scope: Launches agents into the cloud (Warp-host or self-host). Self-hosting and 'own your data' positioning advertised for enterprise control.
products.notes: Newer platform; self-host option stated on marketing site.

products.name: Warp Enterprise
products.data_scope: Adds Zero Data Retention, enforced SSO (Okta), domain verification, enforced telemetry/AI/secret-redaction controls, centralized governance, usage visibility, credit caps, DPA.
products.notes: Strongest compliance/data-control posture; required for ZDR.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium: free tier, paid Pro, and Enterprise (contact sales). Open-source terminal core.
compare.data_residency: United States (GCP). No multi-region/EU residency option documented on own pages.

flags: Privacy policy explicitly lists training/fine-tuning of models supporting AI features as a data-use purpose; AI prompt/input collection is on by default (user-controllable in settings).
Zero Data Retention is gated to the Enterprise plan only; free/Pro users do not get ZDR.
Privacy policy mentions sharing personal information with 'Advertising Partners' (note: marketing data, not stated to be customer code/prompts).
No public bug-bounty program found for the Warp.dev terminal (distinct from Cloudflare WARP).
ISO 27001 and HIPAA not claimed on vendor's own pages; data residency limited to US.
